title: Permission state read-modify-write can lose concurrent updates
reasoning: Each `set` and `delete` call reads the whole JSON file, mutates one permission, and writes the whole file through a fixed temp path. Concurrent permission updates can both read the same old state and then whichever write finishes last overwrites the other update. The shared `${statePath}.tmp` path also means overlapping writes can collide during `writeFile`/`rename`.
reproduction: Start two simultaneous `set` calls for different permission IDs against the same store; both can read the same initial state, then the later rename writes a file containing only one of the two updates.
recommendation: Serialize writes per state path or use an atomic update queue around the read-modify-write sequence. Use unique temporary filenames if concurrent writes remain possible.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for concurrent permission-state writes or preservation of independent permission entries.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that issues concurrent `set` calls for two permission IDs and asserts both entries are present after all promises resolve.
minimumFixScope: Add per-store write serialization in `createPermissionStateStore` and cover concurrent set/delete behavior.
